title: Prefill sanity probes and idempotent replay controller to reduce multi-stream capture flakiness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Investigate and implement a lightweight prefill sanity probe and idempotent replay controller to eliminate intermittent CUDA graph capture/replay failures across concurrent decode streams. Goal is to reduce customer-facing flakiness in multi-stream inference (observed as 1.8% ephemeral decode corruption and replay desyncs under peak load).

Background: Over the past 6 months we've seen sporadic replay mismatches when two or more concurrent decode streams trigger overlapping CUDA Graph captures. Root causes include: racey prefill window alignment, non-deterministic kernel selection under heterogeneous occupancy, and partial KV cache state visible to a capturing stream. Existing mitigations (longer quiesce windows, global capture locks) increase tail latency and reduce throughput.

Scope: Deliver a low-overhead prefill "sanity probe" that validates alignment of critical capture invariants (KV epoch, sequence window checksum, kernel hint set) before committing a capture, and an idempotent replay controller that can safely detect and re-run or skip a replay without polluting shared state. Changes must be backwards compatible with the current capture protocol, and fall back to conservative locking when probes fail.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repro rate for previously flaky mini-bench (40 concurrent streams, mixed seq len) drops from ~1.8% to <0.05%.
- Additional end-to-end median latency overhead from sanity probes <0.8ms on p4d.
- All changes covered by unit + integration tests and performance regression tests in CI.
- Design doc + rollout plan approved by runtime and infra leads.

Deliverables:
- Design doc in Confluence (link below) and a short internal RFC for review.
- Instrumented runtime build with probe toggles and metrics.
- Feature flags: runtime.prefill_probe and runtime.replay_idempotency.
- Canary job template and dashboard updates for replay failure rate and probe hit/miss breakdown.

Constraints & trade-offs: 
- Probes add a small synchronous validation cost prior to capture; we must balance probe coverage vs latency. We'll start with a minimal checksum + epoch test and extend if necessary.
- Full global locking would be simpler but costs throughput; aim for probe+local fencing first and global lock as last-resort fallback.
- Kernel selection nondeterminism stems partly from occupancy heuristics; the probe will record kernel hints but won't change selection policy in v1 to avoid large regressions.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Prefill+Sanity+Probes+and+Idempotent+Replay+Controller
- Investigation notes & repro harness: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1HFlm-prefill-repro-2026
- Example failing run: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/runtime-flaky-replay/3456/console
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892 (WIP, probe scaffolding)
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after triage of customer incident INC-2026-1032. Attached repro harness and initial metrics. Suggested starting with lightweight checksum probe rather than full KV snapshot.

2026-03-11 Marco Ruiz: Built microbench that reproduces ~1.6% replay divergence with 32 streams. Verified divergence correlates with overlapping capture windows and kernel hint flips. Added test to reproduce locally.

2026-03-12 Design review: Runtime leads (K. Huang) and Infra (L. Gomez) prefer probe-first approach. Decision: implement 3-phase probe (epoch, seq-checksum, kernel-hint-stamp). If any probe fails, abort capture and trigger a quiesce + retry path with exponential backoff.

2026-03-13 Marco Ruiz: Implemented probe scaffolding and metrics (probe_hit, probe_fail_reason). Ran noise tests on p4d; median extra cost 0.6ms, 95th percentile 1.4ms. Draft PR opened for initial internal review.

2026-03-14 QA comment (N. Singh): Integration tests show one case where probe passes but replay still mismatches—investigating whether KV epoch granularity is too coarse for certain streaming prefill sizes. Added follow-up task to refine epoch stamping granularity.
2026-03-14 Aisha Patel: Added canary plan — start with 10% of hosted clusters with probe enabled, monitor replay_failure_rate, tail latency, and probe_abort_rate for 48h before wider rollout.
notes: Implementation notes: use CRC32 rolling checksum across the last N KV entries for quick verification; avoid deep copies of KV cache by stamping epochs and ephemeral per-capture token. The replay controller will attempt up to 3 idempotent replays before escalating to a conservative global quiesce path.
qa_checklist: Unit tests for probe logic, integration test with 50-concurrent-stream harness, performance regression job in CI, rollout canary dashboard created
